comment: The one table of the repository-name rule of a stage. A stage lets a run open a pull request only in a CodeCommit repository whose name the rule covers (and that the operator allowed). The rule is a list of 1 to 10 entries. An entry is a repository name (1 to 100 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'), such a prefix of up to 99 characters followed by one '*', or '*' alone. A name is covered when it equals an exact entry, starts with the prefix of a prefix entry, or an entry is '*'. Names are case sensitive. The account-file entry gives the list as `repoNames`; the environment variable `HAMH_REPO_NAMES` (comma separated, spaces around an entry are dropped) wins for one run when it is set and not empty; without either the rule is the default `hamh-e2e-*`. infra/test/repo-names.test.ts runs the rows through infra/lib/repo-names.ts and lib/config.ts `selectTarget`; scripts/tests/test_repo_names.py runs them through scripts/lib/aws_target.py; crates/control-api/tests/repo_names.rs and crates/delivery/tests/repo_names.rs run them through the two Rust copies of the matcher; scripts/tests/test_setup_repo_names.py runs the cover rows through setup.sh. `entry` is merged into a valid account-file entry, `rule` is the list the rule gives, `reason` is the text a refusal carries after `accounts.json accounts[0]: ` (or `HAMH_REPO_NAMES: ` for an environment refusal). `refusal` rows are the exact text of the refusal a Lambda gives for a name the rule does not cover.
